rules.title: Redundant narration comment
rules.repair: Remove comments that merely restate syntax; preserve rationale, constraints, public API notes, and non-obvious intent.

rules.title: Unjustified type escape
rules.repair: Replace broad type escape with a precise type or document a verified boundary reason.

rules.title: Broad exception handling
rules.repair: Narrow the exception scope/type and preserve required error propagation or domain handling.

rules.title: Swallowed exception
rules.repair: Handle, translate, log with purpose, or re-raise the error; do not silently discard failures without an evidenced invariant.

rules.title: Excessive control-flow nesting
rules.repair: Prefer early return/continue or smaller behavior-preserving units when this reduces cognitive load.

rules.title: Single-use abstraction without complexity reduction
rules.repair: Inline or simplify when the abstraction adds indirection without domain meaning, reuse, isolation, or testability benefit.

rules.title: Generic or misleading naming
rules.repair: Use local domain vocabulary and names that expose purpose rather than implementation accident.

rules.title: Repeated logic
rules.repair: Consolidate only when the repeated behavior has the same reason to change; do not force unrelated cases behind a shared abstraction.

rules.title: Dead or unreachable code
rules.repair: Remove verified dead code after confirming no dynamic/plugin/reflection contract depends on it.

rules.title: Weak behavioral assertion
rules.repair: Assert externally meaningful behavior and important failure modes instead of merely mirroring implementation details.

rules.title: Excessive internal mocking
rules.repair: Mock at stable boundaries; avoid coupling tests to internal call choreography unless that choreography is itself contractual.

rules.title: Cleanup conflicts with protected invariant
rules.repair: Do not auto-apply the cleanup. Preserve the invariant and escalate the conflict with evidence.
